target_customer: Oncologists and surgeons who want to know whether residual tumor remains after treatment; later also clinical labs buying COVID-19 test products
problem: After cancer surgery or treatment doctors have limited tests to tell whether tumor cells remain; the company uses RNA based diagnostics and machine learning for residual disease detection.
business_model: Diagnostics tests sold to clinicians and labs; lab kits and software for COVID-19 testing
product_category: RNA diagnostics for minimal residual disease

founders.name: Brandon Steelman
founders.background_notes: Only founder on the YC page; no background found in sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Developing and validating an RNA assay with machine learning for residual tumor detection needs wet lab science, clinical samples and eventually regulatory clearance.

defensibility.rationale: A secondary source reports a granted US patent and a federal grant, which could give some protection, but no trial or FDA record was seen.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sourced evidence of what incumbents did; MRD testing by others grew later but no dated source ties them to this company.

market_need_then: Residual disease detection after cancer treatment is a recognized unmet need according to general MRD sources; no company specific demand evidence was found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand was found, and aggregators confuse it with Clear Genetics.

outcome_analysis: Clear Gene remains listed as active with four people and has little public coverage. The company site shows an RNA residual disease focus plus COVID-19 lab products, and one secondary source says no trial, paper or FDA record backs the science. No funding announcement or exit was found, so the outcome and the reasons are not public in the sources checked.
notes: Funding figures are aggregator only and unverified: PitchBook 150K total, Bouncewatch pre-seed Aug 2018 and seed Dec 2021 undisclosed, CB Insights convertible note with Incite Ventures, Unpopular Ventures and Portfolia. Company site shows supporter logos (YC, Asymmetry, StartX, DV Collective, NIH, NCI) with no amounts. Founding year 2012 on PitchBook conflicts with YC 2018 batch. COVID MICA products date is not stated. No dated competitor sources found near the batch, so the list is empty. YC page location San Francisco versus aggregators San Carlos.
